text: Git branching is a powerful feature that helps teams work together without stepping on each other’s toes. In a typical version control workflow, developers create feature branches to build new ideas or fix bugs in isolation. This keeps the main branch stable and ready for release. Once a feature is complete, a developer can push the branch to a shared repository and open a pull request. This is a request for teammates to review the changes, discuss them, and suggest improvements. After approval, the branch is merged into the main codebase. This process makes collaboration safer, easier to track, and reduces the risk of conflicts.
